Subject: Signer census & template selection — AtlasWorks MSA / Order Form

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to kick off contracting for the AtlasWorks integration. Two quick asks to get your team in motion: 

1) Signer census: I attached a preliminary signer spreadsheet (AtlasWorks_SignerList.xlsx) — can you confirm which signers you need populated (legal vs billing vs technical)? We have multiple subsidiaries and want to make sure the Order Form maps to the right entity.

2) Template choice: we'd like to understand the tradeoffs if we sign Redwood's standard MSA + Order Form vs pushing our template. AtlasWorks legal typically pushes a short set of SLA and data residency asks; if you prefer your template we'll send a party sheet and exhibit requirements.

Attached: AtlasWorks_SignerList.xlsx and a short OrderForm requirements doc.

Goal is to have an initial MSA / Order Form draft out to us by next week. Please confirm next steps and any additional artifacts you need from our side.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Director of Partnerships
AtlasWorks

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 30 Mar 2025 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Signer census & template selection — AtlasWorks MSA / Order Form

Hi Lena — thanks, and welcome on board. Quick responses and a proposed path: 

- Signer census: the attached looks good; for contracting we need a named entity (legal signatory), billing entity, and any reseller/affiliate if relevant. Can you confirm the legal entity to sign the MSA (column B in your sheet)? If subsidiaries will be added later, we can add an Exhibit to cover affiliates.

- Template choice: recommendation is to use Redwood's standard MSA (we attach redwood_template_msa_v2.docx) and capture AtlasWorks-specific commitments in the Order Form / Exhibits. This materially speeds the timeline and reduces redlines. That said, if AtlasWorks has material SLA or data-residency language you must have, please send the clauses early so we can assess impact.

- Questions: 1) Do you require EU data residency or multi-region hosting? 2) Expected monthly seat count and peak concurrency? These inform SLA and hosting exhibit language.

Next steps I'd suggest:
- You confirm the legal/billing signer and return an updated signer sheet.
- We share a draft MSA (our template) + initial Order Form exhibiting seat counts and residency options by EOD Wednesday.
- If helpful, book a 30-min sync (I copied Marissa for scheduling).

Forwarded attachments: redwood_template_msa_v2.docx, OrderForm_Specs_AtlasWorks.pdf

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracting Operations
Redwood Inference

Looping in a quick risk check. Flags I've flagged for Legal/Trust: 
- AtlasWorks called out residency requirements in the intake — if they require EU-only residency for certain data types we need to scope Exhibits and confirm availability in target regions.
- They may request a bespoke SLA (percentile + credits). If so, Legal will need to review; that can add negotiation time.

David — can you confirm what evidence we need from AtlasWorks (SOC2, penetration test report) to move forward with standard templates?

Kimberly — happy to join the sync and help scope the Order Form granularly.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 31 Mar 2025 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Signer census & template selection — AtlasWorks MSA / Order Form

Marissa — for a straightforward standard-template flow we generally need:
- Current SOC 2 Type II report (or a Letter of Attestation)
- Clarification on data residency (which data class — PII, user content, logs — needs to be in-region)
- Expected monthly volumes (tokens/requests) or seat counts for tiering in the Order Form

If AtlasWorks insists on custom SLA language, ask them to share the exact clause(s) and a short rationale — that helps us trade off credits vs latency guarantees.

I'll review the redwood_template_msa_v2.docx and flag any negotiation points by EOD Tuesday.

-David
David Kim
Director, Trust & Security (Contracts)
Redwood Inference
